common_name: Malta Fig (Small Sweet Early-Ripening Mediterranean Heirloom)

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or container trees in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; ripens notably early, giving a reliable crop even in shorter growing seasons.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun. Malta is a small, dark purple-brown Mediterranean heirloom fig grown for ripening notably early in the season, giving gardeners a reliable, dependable crop of sweet, richly flavored fruit even where the growing season isn't long enough for later-ripening varieties to fully mature a full crop. The compact, manageable tree size makes it a practical choice for container culture or smaller garden spaces, and the fruit's small size and thin skin make it excellent for fresh eating straight from the tree, though it does not ship or store as well as firmer, larger fig varieties. As with all figs, protect the roots with heavy mulch in winter in the colder parts of its range, since the top can die back in hard freezes but typically regrows from the root system.

common_name: Yellow Long Neck Fig (Distinctive Elongated Bottleneck-Shaped Heirloom)

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or container trees in spring in well-drained soil in full sun.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun. Yellow Long Neck is a heirloom fig grown as much for its unmistakable, unusual shape as for eating quality, producing fruit with a dramatically elongated, narrow neck tapering to a rounded body, a form so distinctive that a single glance identifies the variety among any collection of figs. Beneath the pale yellow-green skin, the amber-honey flesh is sweet and richly flavored, good for fresh eating, drying, and preserves once the tree is established and producing reliably. The vigorous tree performs well in fig-collector gardens seeking novelty forms alongside more standard varieties, and general fig culture practices — full sun, well-drained soil, and winter root protection in colder zones — apply equally here.

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or container trees in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; bred in Texas for good disease and nematode resistance, making it a strong choice for Gulf Coast gardens.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun. Hunt was developed in Texas and selected for genuinely good resistance to root-knot nematodes and several fig diseases that trouble other varieties in the warm, humid soils of the Gulf South, making it a particularly reliable, low-maintenance choice for Texas, Louisiana, and neighboring Gulf Coast gardens. The medium, brown-skinned fruit has sweet, richly flavored pink-amber flesh, good for fresh eating and preserves, and the productive tree bears a heavy main crop in late summer. Its combination of regional disease resistance and dependable production has made it a long-standing favorite among Gulf Coast home orchardists specifically dealing with the nematode-prone sandy soils common across the region.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun. Lattarula is a classic Italian heirloom fig producing pale yellow-green skinned fruit with intensely sweet, amber-honey colored flesh, considered by many growers to be among the sweetest and most reliably productive of the light-skinned fig varieties widely available in North America. The vigorous, hardy tree sets a good main crop in late summer and often a smaller early crop as well in warm climates, and its productivity and adaptability across a range of soils and conditions have made it a long-standing favorite for both home orchards and small-scale commercial fig growing. As with all figs, provide winter protection for the roots in the colder parts of its range, since the plant reliably regrows from the root system even after top dieback in a hard freeze.

common_name: Black Madeira Fig (Prized Dark-Skinned Strawberry-Red Fleshed Fig)

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or container trees in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; moderate vigor and best adapted to warmer zones with a long growing season.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun. Black Madeira, of Portuguese origin, is prized among serious fig growers as one of the finest-flavored dark fig varieties available, producing deep purple-black skinned fruit that opens to reveal dense, richly colored strawberry-red flesh with an intensely sweet, complex flavor that has earned it a devoted following among fig collectors and specialty growers. The tree has moderate vigor compared to some more rampant fig varieties and performs best with a long, warm growing season to fully ripen its crop and develop peak flavor. Given its more particular growing requirements and somewhat lower yields than workhorse varieties, it is often grown as a specialty or connoisseur's fig alongside more prolific everyday varieties rather than as a primary production tree.
